newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Ten Lesotho police charged after mutiny.
newsitem.headline: Ten Lesotho police charged after mutiny.

text.p: Ten Lesotho police officers were on Friday charged with trying to overthrow the government in an 11-day mutiny which ended in a gunbattle with the army last Sunday.

An indictment read to the accused in a Maseru magistrate's court alleged the policemen sought "to bring the government to its knees and cause its downfall" when they occupied the national police headquarters on February 6.
The accused are part of a group of 100 policemen detained by the Lesotho army after a five-hour battle at the police headquarters in the southern African mountain kingdom's capital early on Sunday.

Court papers also said the rebels refused to lay down their weapons and fired at members of the Lesotho army "who had been lawfully directed to quell the mutiny and to restore order in the administration, operation and running of the Royal Lesotho Mounted Police".

Prosecutor Sipho Mdhuli said he would ask the court at its next hearing on March 7 to order the accused to stand trial in the Lesotho High Court on charges of sedition and contravention of the country's internal security act.
The 10 defendants include officers who are refusing to stand trial for allegedly killing three fellow officers in 1995.
No mention was made of the other 90 detained.
The leader of the renegade band, Lieutenant Pakiso Molise, is still on the run from police, who have extended their search across the border into South Africa.

The Lesotho government, headed by ageing Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle, said earlier this week Molise had sought refuge at the palace of Lesotho's King Lestsie III after the raid but fled as the army closed in on him.
The government said it was shocked to learn that the palace had allowed Molise to take refuge there.
Letsie, with the support of the army and police, dismissed Mokhehle and his cabinet in a royal coup in August 1994.
Mokhehle, 78, was reinstated a month later after intervention by southern African leaders led by South Africa's Nelson Mandela.
